results.references: - Artem Agafonov, Aslan Ashabokov, Dmitry Kamzolov, Alexander D’yakonov, Alexander Gasnikov, and Martin Takáč. [Matching the Lower Bounds: Stochastic Contracting Cubic Newton and Its Optimal Acceleration](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.11693v2). 2026 preprint, v2 (October 13; first submitted October 8). Complexity: $O(1+(\sigma_gD/\varepsilon)^2+\sqrt{\sigma_hD^2/\varepsilon}+(\rho D^3/\varepsilon)^{2/7})$ total stochastic gradient and Hessian oracle calls for $\mathbb E[f(w_T)-f^*]\le\varepsilon$, using Accelerated Stochastic Contracting Cubic Newton with known noise bounds; fixed cost of two gradient calls and one Hessian call per iteration.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a globally convex, differentiable function over a convex body C in Euclidean space, with a minimizer xstar in C. The gradient is differentiable and the Hessian is ρ-Lipschitz on C; strong convexity is not required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A gradient query returns g(x,ω), with E[g(x,ω)]=∇f(x) and E[‖g(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖²]≤σg² on C. Each call uses a fresh IID seed.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: A Hessian query returns a full symmetric PSD operator H(x,ω), with E[‖H(x,ω)−∇²f(x)‖op²]≤σh² on C. Hessian unbiasedness is not required. Each call selects either a gradient or a Hessian; no function values are supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Gradient variance is bounded by σg²; Hessian mean-square operator-norm error is bounded by σh². Only second moments are required, with σg,σh≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: Hessian estimates may be biased, while every returned Hessian must be symmetric PSD. Gradient estimates must be unbiased.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is ℝ^d with Euclidean norm; Hessian errors use the induced operator norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information comprises d, C, x0, D, ρ, and σg. The Hessian error bound σh and accuracy ε are hidden from algorithm construction, although they determine the execution budget. D,ρ,ε>0, x0∈C, and diam(C)≤D. Hessian Lipschitz continuity is required only on C.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must satisfy E[f(output)−f(xstar)]≤ε, with an integrable objective gap and measurable output.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output belongs to C for every random realization.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The objective guarantee averages over algorithm randomness and IID oracle randomness under a fixed total oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The convex constrained objective is standard, but the combination of potentially biased PSD Hessian estimates, an unknown Hessian error bound, and separate stochastic derivative queries defines a specialized oracle formulation.
